observations.text: Re-approval scope and byte state at the new commit. argv "git rev-parse HEAD" prints c274df821da41888915de19488ad4d51ffe1abb4, exit 0; argv "git status --porcelain" prints only "?? docs/feature/iis-secrets-key-replace/.nwdes-drafts/", the draft directory of another reviewer, so every judged oracle and support file is judged by its committed bytes and the tree is clean for them. This is a re-approval of the same S1 oracle, forced by the candidate refusal "OracleChanged: S1", not a first review: the accepted record of this subject names c03bed6, and S2 and S3 have since added to the three files S1 shares with them. Mechanical selection of the test files changed since that approved revision: argv "git diff --numstat c03bed6 HEAD -- crates/foundry-acceptance/", exit 0, names exactly three files and their line counts - src/steps/feature_instance_integration_setup.rs 30 added / 0 deleted, src/support/instance_integration_setup.rs 181 / 0, tests/features/instance-integration-setup.feature 183 / 2. The fourth declared support, crates/foundry-acceptance/src/support/external_integration_plugins.rs, is absent from that list, so it is unchanged and the reviewed set is complete. Nothing outside those three files is in scope for this round.

No S1 scenario was removed or weakened; the S1 region of the oracle is byte-identical. argv: a python3 block that loads the feature file at c03bed6 and at HEAD with "git show", splits both into scenario blocks and compares the body of each of the six S1 locators of the acceptance record. Output, exit 0: "scenarios at c03bed6: 93 at HEAD: 100", "removed scenarios: []", and IDENTICAL for all six - "Replacing the secrets key seals every saved credential again and nobody reconnects" (line 1070), "The replace page says how many saved credentials are sealed again, and reading it replaces nothing" (1114), "Confirming the replacement says how many credentials are now sealed under the new key" (1134), "A reload after the replacement reads the page with no notice and claims no second replacement" (1153), "Two replace requests at the same moment replace the key once, and every replica opens every credential" (1167), "After a replacement the operator's own key rotation still leaves every credential opening" (1183). The seven added scenarios are all S3 start-over work, the first of them at line 1202. Whole-region confirmation rather than per-scenario only: argv "git show c03bed6:...feature | sed -n 1,1200p | shasum -a 256" and argv "sed -n 1,1200p ...feature | shasum -a 256" both print 54520e063d22cc9d9eb6c3523f9df6a5eed286ffb3100424ce6e0310d3e17efc, the same digest recorded in observation R8 of the accepted round, and line 1200 lies inside the comment of the first S3 scenario, so the digest spans every S1 scenario and every line between them. argv "git diff c03bed6 HEAD -- crates/foundry-acceptance/ | grep ^-[^-]" prints exactly two lines, exit 0: the two prose comment lines above the S3 scenario at feature line 1341, reworded in place. No assertion, step text, Examples row or tag was deleted anywhere in the delta.

The two support files S1 depends on changed only by appending, so no step S1 drives changed its meaning. argv "git diff c03bed6 HEAD -- crates/foundry-acceptance/src/steps/feature_instance_integration_setup.rs crates/foundry-acceptance/src/support/instance_integration_setup.rs", exit 0: two hunks, zero deleted lines. The steps hunk is "@@ -752,3 +752,33 @@" at the end of the file - six new bindings, all start-over texts ("types ... and chooses Start over on the start over page", "has started over with a new secrets key", "the stored secrets key is one this Foundry opens", "reads no connection as connected", "that second Foundry server has said nothing for a minute", "says again that it opens the stored secrets key"), none of which is a step text of any S1 scenario. The support hunk is "@@ -3218,6 +3218,187 @@", inserted between given_other_server_stopped and the "a minute passes" function: it adds only top-level items - GENERATED_NOTICE, CONFIRMATION, struct TypedForm, typed_form, choose_on_start_over_page, when_type_and_start_over, given_started_over, then_key_started_over, then_no_connection_connected, given_other_server_quiet_for_a_minute, when_other_server_speaks_again. No line was added inside the body of an existing function, so remember(), then_nothing_replaced, when_open_replace, when_choose_key_control, then_on_replace_page, eip::follow and every other function the S1 scenarios reach are the exact bytes the accepted round judged. The r1 remediation step at feature line 1119 and its config-version strengthening (observations R3 and R4) therefore stand unchanged.

The added step bindings introduce no ambiguous or shadowing match for an S1 step, and the S1 scenarios still execute and still observe their outcomes at HEAD. Evidence supplied by the host rather than re-executed, as the inputs of the S1 judgments are unchanged (observations R10 and R11). At 9a9908a, with S3 production still absent, the lane log /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jeffbailey-Projects-canzan-foundry/ae6f0864-8ca5-43d5-b970-fb78c37ae831/scratchpad/lane-us-iis-07.S3.txt reads "29 scenarios (20 passed, 9 failed)", "451 steps (442 passed, 9 failed)" and "acceptance run failed: 9 step(s) failed, 0 parsing error(s), 0 hook error(s)"; the nine failures are all 405 on the start-over POST, missing S3 production behaviour, and zero parsing and zero hook errors establish mechanically that the six new step regexes left every S1 step text with exactly one binding. At HEAD c274df8 the log /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jeffbailey-Projects-canzan-foundry/ae6f0864-8ca5-43d5-b970-fb78c37ae831/scratchpad/reviewer-lane-us-iis-07.c274df8.log reads "29 scenarios (29 passed)" and "513 steps (513 passed)", exit 0. argv "grep -n" over that log for the six S1 titles prints all eleven S1 scenario executions - the walking scenario at log line 15, the four counts of the replace-page outline at 61, 82, 103 and 124, the three counts of the confirm outline at 145, 163 and 181, the reload at 199, the two-replica race at 221 and the CLI rotation at 245 - and argv "grep -c" for failure markers over the same log prints 0. The S1 rows are the same eleven executions the accepted round observed, still present and still passing beside seven S3 scenarios.

No new execution is claimed and no S1 semantic RED is restated as new. The current comparison justifying reuse: the S1 region of the oracle and both changed supports are unchanged against the revision of the accepted round (observations R10 and R11), and the declared production files of S1 shipped before it, so no affected check has to run again at c274df8; the two lane logs cited in R12 are runs the host executed, named with their revision, not this reviewer restamping its own earlier output. The S1 semantic RED stays the measured one cited in observation R2 of the accepted record: ~/.cache/nwdes/iis-secrets-key-replace/s1-red-2.txt, exit 101, eleven of eleven S1 scenarios failing on the replace door answering 404 Not Found through the production router at /admin/instance/integrations/secrets-key/replace, which is the missing-behaviour failure the S1 promises name and not an import, collection or fixture failure. S1 production shipped at d34ab3a, so that RED cannot be observed again at HEAD and none is invented here: the GREEN of R12 is the completion observation of that recorded RED. The S1 acceptance rows themselves did not move: argv "git diff c03bed6 HEAD -- docs/feature/iis-secrets-key-replace/acceptance.md | grep ^@@" prints hunks at 331, 419, 437 and 445 only, while argv "grep -n ^### S docs/feature/iis-secrets-key-replace/acceptance.md" places S1 at lines 5-229, S2 at 230 and S3 at 448. Every retained judgment of the accepted round therefore holds unchanged: criteria adequacy against the agreed value, the driving-port boundary, closure for E1-E6, E8-E10, E23, E24 and the justified NotTested at the public port for P3, whose two halves remain completion obligations of DELIVER.

typesafe: unavailable at this revision, as in the accepted round. argv "zsh -lc 'if [ -n \"$TYPESAFE_API_KEY\" ]; then echo KEY_PRESENT; else echo KEY_ABSENT; fi'" prints KEY_ABSENT, exit 0, so the service prerequisite is absent from the login environment and no call was attempted or fabricated; no producer-owned judgment was reused. The only question of this round - whether the delta removes or weakens an S1 observation - is mechanical and was answered with git and shasum, not with a semantic service. No timing claim is made: no S1 test is at half budget and no derogation is in force, so no nine-run measurement was taken. Capability limit retained: this round observed no new execution of its own, and its confidence in S1 behaviour at HEAD rests on the host-supplied lane logs of 9a9908a and c274df8 together with the byte identity of the S1 region and its supports.

diagnostic:

The added step regexes shadow no S1 step: the S3 lane at 9a9908a reports 0 parsing and 0 hook errors with its nine failures all 405 on the start-over POST, and the lane at c274df8 reports 29 of 29 scenarios and 513 of 513 steps, exit 0, with all eleven S1 scenario executions present and no failure marker.

No new execution and no invented RED. The S1 semantic RED remains the measured one of the record - eleven of eleven S1 scenarios failing on the replace door answering 404 through the production router, exit 101 - which cannot recur now that S1 production shipped at d34ab3a; the GREEN at HEAD is that RED's completion observation. No S1 acceptance row moved: every acceptance.md hunk sits at line 331 or above while S1 occupies lines 5 to 229. Criteria adequacy against the agreed value, the driving-port boundary, and closure for E1-E6, E8-E10, E23, E24 are retained, as is the justified NotTested at the public port for P3, whose two halves stay completion obligations of DELIVER. typesafe: unavailable, key absent; the one question of this round was mechanical.
